subject: Acme POC — next steps & eval methodology alignment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme POC — next steps & proposed eval plan

Thanks again for the time today, Tom and Priya — great discussion. Quick recap from our discovery + proposed next steps so we can align on a concrete POC plan: 

Recap / goals
- Primary goal: validate Redwood inference for Acme search assistant (latency, correctness, and hallucination rate) on your live-ish workload.
- Primary users: internal support agents + knowledge base retrieval flows.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm or edit):
1) Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end under 200ms for single-turn queries (on Dedicated config).
2) Accuracy: top-1 answer correctness >= 85% measured on a curated testset agreed before kickoff.
3) Hallucinations: <5% of sampled outputs flagged as hallucinations by manual review.
4) Operational: logs, KV cache hit metrics, and token-level billing visible in Redwood Console.

Evaluation approach (high level)
- Phase A (offline evals): run curated testset against candidate models, apply grading rubric (attached).
- Phase B (shadow/online): 2-week shadow run on a subset of traffic (1-5%) to validate latency and behavior in prod-like conditions.

Proposed timeline
- Kickoff & data handoff: week of Oct 12
- Offline evals complete: Oct 19
- Shadow run: Oct 21 — Nov 4
- Final review & recommendations: Nov 8

Ownership (proposed)
- Acme: provide sample dataset, annotator access, and security/compliance contact (Priya).
- Redwood: Marissa (project lead) + Dev (integration & instrumentation) + Rachel (eval methodology / rubric).

Attachments: acme_poc_plan_v1.pdf (POC plan), evaluation_rubric_v1.xlsx (detailed grading matrix), acme_sample_dataset.csv (sample rows)

Please confirm the success criteria and timeline, and if you prefer any changes to the offline/online split. If that looks good I’ll update the POC plan and lock owners.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecorp.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC — next steps & proposed eval plan

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Overall this matches our internal expectations. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Success criteria adjustments:
- Latency: can we make the target 95th percentile < 250ms to start? Our infra has a bit more variability; 200ms is ideal but 250ms is acceptable for the POC.
- Accuracy: 85% top-1 is fine as a pass threshold. We’d like an additional metric: top-3 should be >95% to capture near-miss usefulness.
- Hallucinations: agree on <5% as measured on random sample of 500 queries.

2) Evaluation approach: we prefer starting with the offline evals (gives us a baseline) and then a 2-week shadow on a non-critical slice of traffic (support web widget). Shadow at 2% traffic initially, ramp to 5% in week 2 if everything looks stable.

3) Timeline: kickoff on Oct 13 works better for our team (we have a release window Oct 9–12). Can you shift the dates by one week?

4) Data & security: Priya will coordinate how we can share the sample dataset and any NDA/SCAs required.

If you can update the plan with the small timeline shift and latency threshold relaxed to 250ms, we’ll sign off and hand over the dataset next week.

—Tom
Tom Harris
Head of Platform, Acme Corp

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@acmecorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme POC — next steps & proposed eval plan

Thanks Tom — good notes. Quick note from the eval/quality side about methodology so we’re all aligned before data handoff.

Proposed eval methodology (detailed):
A) Offline evals (deterministic, reproducible) — deliverables:
- Use provided sample dataset (we ask for ~2k-5k representative queries + ground truth where available).
- Apply the attached evaluation_rubric_v1.xlsx: each query gets labels for relevance (0/1), factuality (0/1), and severity if hallucination (low/med/high).
- Metrics reported: top-1 accuracy, top-3 accuracy, hallucination rate, average response length, token consumption.
- Controlled runs across 3 candidate model configs (e.g., base, quantized, low-latency).

B) Online shadow (real traffic, behavioral):
- Run shadow at 2% traffic for 7 days, then 5% for next 7 days if stable (as Tom proposed).
- Collect production telemetry: end-to-end latency, server-side latency, error rates, and user engagement signals (CTR on suggested answers if available).
- Sampling and privacy: redact PII before exporting logs; Acme security to confirm masking rules.

C) Grading rubric (how we interpret pass/fail):
- Pass if: top-1 >= 85% AND top-3 >= 95% AND hallucination rate <= 5% AND 95p latency <= 250ms.
- Tiered recommendations if near-threshold: provide quantization or model variant recommendations and estimated cost delta.

D) Ownership & instrumentation:
- Acme: provide dataset, define PII redaction policy, share a small set of representative production logs (sanitized).
- Redwood (Dev): confirm we can ingest logs for shadowing (Dev, can you confirm instrumentation endpoints + required headers?), and enable per-request tracing in the Console.

E) Deliverables & reporting:
- Weekly status notes during eval window, final report with metrics, example failures, and recommended next model/version.

Dev — can you confirm you can enable the shadowing hooks and capture the fields listed (request_id, response_time_ms, model_variant, prompt_hash, token_count)? If not, list what’s feasible so we can tweak the rubric.

I’ll start the offline eval skeleton once we have the dataset and masking rules.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Applied ML — Evaluations
